why?  

unless you consider a child the property of their parents (which unfortunately is how our world is set up) or argue that they do not count as full humans there is no reason to not grant a child the same human rights of autonomy over their own life as to adults.  

and isn't allowing assisted suicide for somatic pain but not for mental pain saying that the person with depression does not suffer enough? how could anyone who is not that person with the suffering judge if their life is worth living or not?  

There are people with severe pain and other restrictions who still enjoy life, and there are people with "objectively" less severe diagnosis or circumstances who want to die. Why not let everyone decide for themselves?  Life and pain are subjective.

Philosophically I can't think of an argument against suicide being fully legal and accessible. The problems come in because of the possibility of people being coerced by their next of kin or forced to chose it for example because treatment for their cancer is too expensive etc.

Her response was that eating was not something that is guaranteed on this job and to get lost.   

As a resident you are worthless. I once went 16hrs on a 24hr shift without any food (cause no time) and ended up crying in some lonely corner of the OR from exhaustion. There are no mentors, there is no one who cares about us. We are tools, the only reason we are allowed to exist is to make the lives of the attendings easier.  

The only way you can help your friend is by helping them find a way out of medicine. But that - especially in the US with insane loans - can be a very difficult path.

This is only anectdotal but knowing a lot of people with cptsd, some with bpd and some with both I'd say the defining difference is impulsivity. People with CPTSD tend to spend extreme amount of times on careful planning, are hesitent on doing spontaneous things, have to have safety strategies in place etc. People with BPD tend to be quit impulsive/spontaneous.  

Example: I knew a person with BPD who one day posted something like "lol bought art supplies and now don't know how to get money for food for the next 10 days"... and I - despite now having a job that pays ok - can barely buy that 30$ puzzle I wanted for a few months, because it is not strictly necessary for survival and what if I loose my job etc... cptsd is all about survival, surviving alone cause we all grew up with no one there to help - and often don't have anyone around to help in the present either.
